headline: High: shared filesystem writes and shared-context skills create medium-to-high risks of leakage, conflict, and cascading errors; prompt injection is low because no direct channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct ingestion channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and marketingskills, so prompt injection is not default. However, marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skills and file surfaces, and awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source that could be manually copied into B. That makes only a low-risk copy/paste bridge plausible.
conditions: IF an operator copies awesome-selfhosted content into marketingskills prompts or skill files
IF marketingskills treats copied content as instructions rather than reference material
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Paste only quoted excerpts, not whole files
Add a one-line provenance header to copied content
Review copied content for imperative language before use

B_data_leakage.rationale: marketingskills has read/write filesystem access and explicit file surfaces, while awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source with no stated isolation or sandboxing. If A's curated content is placed into B's workspace, B can read and potentially transmit it via allowlisted network egress. The pairwise leakage path exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted content is stored in a directory readable by marketingskills
IF marketingskills sends workspace files or context to GitHub or marketing-skills.com
mitigations: Store A and B data in separate directories
Disable file ingestion for sensitive A content
Use a redacted copy of A for B
Audit outbound requests from B for file payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable, so it cannot write; marketingskills can read/write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, with multiple instances supported. There is no direct write-write conflict, but B can still contend with shared files or generated artifacts if the operator places both in one workspace. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF marketingskills instances modify the same files without external locking
mitigations: Assign unique output directories per agent
Run only one marketingskills instance per workspace
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Make A read-only in the shared environment

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around skills that reference each other and build on shared context, so it may treat upstream material as authoritative. awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge source, which B could render into marketing outputs without verification. That creates a default pathway where A's content can cascade into B's downstream work products.
conditions: IF marketingskills uses A-derived content as source material for generated marketing copy
IF no human verification step checks factual claims before publication
mitigations: Require human review before publishing B outputs
Add a verification checklist for A-derived claims
Tag A content as reference-only in B prompts
Block direct copy-forward from A into final drafts

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-selfhosted, and marketingskills only shows marketing-content handling plus allowlisted egress. The pair therefore has only a limited compliance surface, mainly if operators move regulated data into B. Because the other agent is not shown to process regulated data, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into marketingskills workflows
IF B's allowlisted outbound destinations are used for that regulated data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B workflows
Use synthetic or anonymized examples
Document retention expectations for B outputs
Review outbound destinations before use
